title: Isolation-based Spherical Ensemble Representations for Tabular Anomaly Detection
summary: Unsupervised tabular anomaly detection is challenged by conflicting distributional assumptions, computational inefficiency, and difficulty handling diverse anomaly types. ISER builds spherical partition ensembles from random subsets, encodes each point by hypersphere radii as a monotonic local-density proxy, and scores with either average-based or cosine-similarity-based comparison to an all-ones anomaly reference; ISER-IF applies iForest to this transformed representation with an inverted scoring function. ISER-S reaches average AUC-ROC 0.8523 over 20 datasets, and ISER-IF improves iForest Ionosphere AUC-ROC from 0.8530 to 0.9314 (+9.19%).

match_target.why: User hinted Table IV, ISER-IF AUC-ROC on Ionosphere. C1 is exactly that value; Ionosphere has only 351 points, so this is the cheapest run that still demonstrates the paper's central ISER-IF enhancement.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUC-ROC is bounded in [0,1], Ionosphere has 351 examples (<2,000), and the paper prints AUC as a fraction. No std/CI is reported for Table IV, so use 0.02 absolute.

requirements.stmt: For each of t partitionings, randomly sample ψ points from D without replacement to form Di.
requirements.quote: Randomly sample ψ points from D without replacement

requirements.stmt: For every sampled center z, set hypersphere radius to the distance to its nearest neighbor within Di\{z}.
For a query x and partitioning Hi, identify all covering hyperspheres Ci(x)={z in Di : ∥x−z∥≤r[z]} and select the covering one with smallest radius.
requirements.quote: we select the covering hypersphere with the smallest radius

requirements.stmt: Encode φi(x)=1−1/r[ẑi(x)] when x is covered; otherwise set φi(x)=1.
requirements.quote: we assign φi(x) = 1, indicating that the point is not covered by any hyperspheres in this partitioning

requirements.stmt: Concatenate φi(x) for i=1..t into the ensemble representation Φ(x) in R^t.
requirements.quote: The ensemble representation of point x is constructed by concatenating the coverage indicators from all t partitionings

requirements.stmt: ISER-A anomaly score is Savg(x)=1/t Σ Φi(x).
requirements.quote: The average-based anomaly score is computed as the arithmetic mean of all ensemble components

requirements.stmt: ISER-S anomaly score is Ssim(x)=sim(Φ(x), 1) with all-ones reference vector.
requirements.quote: The similarity-based anomaly score is computed using cosine similarity between the point’s ensemble representation and the anomaly reference vector

requirements.stmt: ISER-IF applies iForest to the transformed feature space Φ(x).
requirements.quote: we apply iForest to the transformed feature space Φ(x)

requirements.stmt: ISER-IF replaces iForest score with SISER-IF(x,n)=1−2^{−E(h(Φ(x)))/c(n)}.
requirements.quote: To accommodate this inversion, we modify the original iForest anomaly scoring function [11] as:

requirements.stmt: Use default t=200; search ψ in {2^m, m=1..8} for ISER, iForest, iNNE, IDK, ADERH.
requirements.quote: For iForest, iNNE, IDK, ADERH and proposed methods, ψ ∈{2m, m = 1, 2, . . . , 8} and with default t = 200.
We use Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC-ROC) as evaluation metrics.

requirements.stmt: Repeat each experiment 5 times and report the average.
requirements.quote: Each experiment is repeated 5 times and reported average results.

requirements.stmt: Evaluate in the unsupervised setting on the full contaminated dataset, with both normal and anomalous instances available during training.
requirements.quote: our experiments assume access to the entire dataset containing both normal and anomalous instances during training
